issues.failure_explanation: Under (i)-(ii) only, lambda_k is the eigenvalue of Q for f_k, not for e_k. Var<W_Q(t),e_k> = t<Qe_k,e_k>, which need not equal t*lambda_k, so omega_k = lambda_k^{-1/2}<W_Q,e_k> need not be a standard Wiener process. The 'by definition' claim is unsupported; the variance identity requires Qe_k = lambda_k e_k, i.e. (iii).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Assume (iii) (and lambda_k > 0) for the Wiener-process claim, and justify the variance via Qe_k = lambda_k e_k.
issues.overall_effect: The first conclusion of the lemma is false under its stated hypotheses. Later results assume the full Assumption and are unaffected.
issues.title: Standard-Wiener property of omega_k claimed without the joint-eigenbasis hypothesis (iii)
issues.why_classification: Adding one standard hypothesis that every downstream use already assumes preserves all claims.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: satisfy the bounds $r^{-1} C_\Delta k^{\frac{2 \alpha}{d}}\leq \mu_k$ and $\lambda_k \leq \sigma r^{-\gamma} C_\Delta k^{- \frac{2 \beta}{d}}$

issues.failure_explanation: From xi_k >= C_Delta k^{2/d} one gets mu_k >= r^{-1} C_Delta^alpha k^{2alpha/d} and lambda_k <= sigma r^{-gamma} C_Delta^{-beta} k^{-2beta/d}, not the stated bounds. The stated constant should carry C_Delta^{-beta-(2gamma-1)alpha}. Since any smaller C_Delta is also admissible, for gamma<1 the stated constant tends to 0 as C_Delta -> 0 while the error stays fixed, so the stated bound is false.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use C_1 = r^{-1}C_Delta^alpha and C_2 = sigma r^{-gamma} C_Delta^{-beta}, and recompute C accordingly.
issues.overall_effect: The explicit error constant of the corollary is wrong; the rate M^{-2nu/d} is unaffected.
issues.title: Wrong constants C_1, C_2 make the explicit corollary constant incorrect
issues.why_classification: A local recomputation of constants preserves the rate and the method.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof bounds (E|c_k - c~_k|^2)^{1/2} by (sqrt(lambda_k)/Gamma(gamma)) C delta h^{...}. Squaring gives lambda_k, mu_k^{-2/q} and delta^2 = (1+sqrt(log(t/h)))^2, not sqrt(lambda_k), mu_k^{-1/q} and delta. The error is exactly proportional to lambda_k, so a bound linear in sqrt(lambda_k) with lambda-independent C fails for large lambda_k. At gamma = m+3/2 the squared L2-best-approximation error is of order h^{2m+2} log(1/h), exceeding the claimed h^{2m+2} sqrt(log). The main theorem inherits the unsquared delta.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate with lambda_k, mu_k^{-2/q} and delta_{gamma,h}^2 (log factor log(t/h)) in thm-convergence and its corollaries, and use delta^2 in thm:main-result.
issues.overall_effect: The stated mean-square temporal error bounds (lambda_k- and mu_k-dependence, critical log factor) are not established and are partly false. The same applies to the corollaries and the full-discretisation theorem.
issues.title: Mean-square bound states unsquared prefactors (sqrt(lambda_k), mu_k^{-1/q}, delta) though the proof bounds the RMS
issues.why_classification: The rates survive, but stated guarantees (lambda-scaling, critical-case log factor) must be weakened across four results.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: We can use an almost identical argument to show that

issues.failure_explanation: Comparability of each term of a difference (via lem:boundedness-p0-inequalities, with different constants) does not make the difference comparable to the difference of the comparators. The cross terms 2*alpha*g_l(...) have arbitrary sign, so 'lesssim' bounds reverse when alpha*g_l < 0. Termwise bounds with one constant also do not bound a sum with cancellation. The key case h = g - f_t with g close to f_t is exactly such a near-cancellation. The stability estimate is therefore not proved.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Prove the bound cellwise: on each cell, minimise ||c + alpha*phi||^2 over alpha with phi = f - f(s~_l). Cauchy-Schwarz with phi non-constant gives a ratio bounded uniformly in terms of theta, gamma and kbar (by scaling/compactness, the last cell needing theta<1 or gamma>=1). Then sum over cells.
issues.overall_effect: The boundedness hypothesis of thm-convergence for the left-point/theta-method is unproven, so the convergence result for the order-0 scheme lacks support.
issues.title: Invalid term-by-term comparison in proof of L2-stability of the point-evaluation operator Pi_0
issues.why_classification: The statement appears true, but a replacement argument is needed; the result survives with a contained new proof.

issues.failure_explanation: Bounded inverse only means mu_k >= c > 0; summability of mu_k^{-1} is trace-class. For the paper's operators, mu_k ~ k^{2alpha/d}, so the sum diverges whenever 2alpha <= d, e.g. the paper's sphere example (d=2, alpha=0.5). The claimed boundedness of C''_M 'assuming only that Q is bounded' therefore fails in the paper's own typical regimes.

failure_location.quote: In most practical applications $A$ will have bounded inverse, i.e., $\sum_{k = 1}^M \mu_k^{-1} < \infty$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace with the correct condition (A^{-1} trace class, i.e. 2alpha > d for the model operators) and drop the 'most practical applications' claim.
issues.overall_effect: Misleading claim about when the temporal error constant is uniform in M.
issues.title: False claim that bounded inverse means summable mu_k^{-1} in most applications
issues.why_classification: A prose correction; no formal result depends on it.

For nu_s=nu_t=1, beta_s=beta^*=0.5 it gives alpha=1, while the example uses alpha=0.5. Also, r=10, kappa=2.828, alpha=0.5, gamma=1.5 give r_t=10 by the stated formula, not 5.0.
